items.text: Covering as an axiom
$(f_i\colon X_i\to Y)$ epimorphic in $R_2$ (covering): require $(\varphi(f_i))$ covering in $E$.
\textstyle\coprod_i X_i\xrightarrow{\ \alpha\ }Y\quad\text{covering}
$\alpha$ epimorphic $\iff$ the diagonal $Y\sqcup_{\coprod X_i}Y\to Y$ is an isomorphism.
Y\sqcup_{\coprod X_i}Y\;\xrightarrow{\ \sim\ }\;Y\qquad\text{(arrow between constructions in }R_2)
Restrict to the structures in $T(E)$ turning this arrow into an isomorphism.
Algebraic structures in topoi are topoi
Geometrically, arrows between theories go the same way as arrows between topoi. Works if only finite inverse limits are used — no infinite products.
Example: the empty structure on one object
What axioms can be put on one object without any arrow? The classifying topos $B$ and its subtopoi.
$I$ = one point = one unspecified object $X$. Add products: the $X^n$, maps = projections only ($n=0$ allowed).
J=\{X^n\}\simeq(\text{finite sets, empty one included})^{\circ},\qquad B=\widehat J
Covariant functors finite sets $\to$ sets: augmented simplicial sets.
Points of $B$
\operatorname{pts}(B_T)=\operatorname{Hom}(P,B_T)=T(\mathbf{Ens})
Categories $T(E)=\operatorname{Hom}_\Delta(B_T,E)$ have filtering direct limits (finite limits commute with filtering colimits in a topos).
Points of $B$ = set-theoretic realisations (opposite category) = fibre functors.
The points of real interest: of finite presentation = essential points, those represented by the $X^n$:
\Delta_0,\Delta_1,\dots,\Delta_n,\dots\quad\text{(standard simplices; I write the points } X^n)
Here subtopoi are known by the points they contain: the smallest subtopos containing given points inverts the arrows whose fibres at those points are isomorphisms.
Subtopoi of $\widehat J$ = topologies on $J$; fibre products exist, so pretopologies suffice. Diagram of results:
Subtopoi of $B$ and their finite points
B:\ \mathbb N\qquad\qquad B^{*}:\ \mathbb N^{*}\ \ (n\neq0)
Open subtopoi = subobjects of the final object $e_B$: only three canonical ones: empty, $e_B$ itself, and the image of $f\colon X\to e_B$.
\Phi_0:\ \{0\}\quad\text{(closed complement of }B^*)
T_B(E)=\{\text{objects } x\in E\}\ \ (\text{no restriction})
T_{B^*}(E)=\{x\in E:\ x\to e\ \text{epimorphic}\}\qquad(\text{sets: non-empty})
The one-point-closed subtopos $\Phi_0$: sets with zero elements.
T_{\varnothing}(E)=\begin{cases}\{*\}&E\ \text{empty}\\ \varnothing&E\ \text{non-empty}\end{cases}
T_{\Phi_0}(E)=\{x:\ \varnothing_E\xrightarrow{\sim}x\}\ \simeq\ \text{one-point category}
$\Phi_{01}$: the subtopos with exactly the points $0$ and $1$.
T_{\Phi_{01}}(E)=\{\text{subobjects of the final object}\}\qquad(\text{sets with at most one point})
Two points but not a discrete topos.
\Phi_1=\Phi_{01}\cap B^{*}:\ \text{finite point }\{1\}
T_{\Phi_1}(E)=\{\text{final objects of }E\}\ \simeq\ \text{one-point category}
$\Phi_1$ and $\Phi_0$ are both the one-point topos, but they are two different points of $B$.
$B^{*}$: cosimplicial-type sets (functors from non-empty finite sets).
The topos $\widehat{\Delta_1}$
$\Delta_1$: two objects, one arrow between them. $\widehat{\Delta_1}$ = pairs of sets with a map.
Functors $\Delta_1\to E$: two objects $x,y$ and an arrow. Left exact: the target is the final object and the arrow is a monomorphism.
\widehat{\Delta_1}=\operatorname{Top}(\Delta_1),\qquad \Delta_1=\text{space with 2 points, one closed, one open}
The spectrum of a discrete valuation ring.
A morphism of a topos into this space = an open subset of the topos (a subobject of the final object). A cogenerator for spaces, replacing the real line for non-separated spaces.
Subtopoi form a lattice: arbitrary intersections and sups.
Exercises
Two objects, no structure: subtopoi from $X$, from $Y$, intersections — and conditions on $X\times Y$ (e.g. empty)?
Two objects and an arrow $X\to Y$: conditions on $X$, on $Y$, on the pair, on the arrow.
An object with an endomorphism.
X\times Y\to Z\qquad\text{(composition law on three sets)}
X\times Y\to Y\qquad\text{(operation)}
A composition law on $X$: groups etc. — probably too many subtopoi to list.
Classifying topos for groups, explicitly
$\Sigma$ = groups of finite presentation, $r=\Sigma^{\circ}$. The universal group in $r$ is $\mathbb Z$.
Group structure on $\mathbb Z$ in $r$ = cogroup structure in $\Sigma$:
\mathbb Z\to\mathbb Z*\mathbb Z,\qquad e\mapsto e_1e_2
R=\widehat r,\qquad \text{group structures in }E=\operatorname{Hom}_{\mathrm{lex}}(r,E)=\operatorname{Hom}_\Delta(R,E)
Classifying topos of a single group $G$
$C$ = one object, endomorphisms $G$. A functor $C\to E$ = an object $X$ of $E$ with $G$-action.
$\widehat C=B_G$: sets with $G$-action.
To $P\in B_G$ associate the contracted product:
P\wedge^{G}X=(P\times X)/G,\qquad (p,x)\cdot g=(pg,\,g^{-1}x)
(pg,x)\sim(p,gx)
Equivalence: objects with $G$-action $\leftrightarrow$ continuous functors $\widehat C\to E$ commuting with direct limits.
Left exact iff $X$ is a torsor under the constant group $G_E$.
So $\widehat C$ classifies $G$-torsors over a variable topos.
